samples.text:
Because of the internet, many people can now work from home, and some of them decide to leave big cities and move to small towns or the countryside. I think this is a positive development for the people and also for the country.

The main benefit is for the people who move. Life in a big city is very expensive and stressful. Rent is high, the traffic is terrible and there is a lot of noise and pollution. In a small town, people can rent or buy a bigger house with a garden for less money, and they can enjoy fresh air and nature. This make their life healthier and more relaxing, especially for families with children.

Another benefit is for the small towns. In many countries, young people have left the countryside to find jobs in the city, so villages become empty and shops and schools close. When remote workers move there, they spend their money in local shops and cafes, and the town become more alive again. Also, big cities become less crowded, which help to reduce traffic and pollution.

However, this change can cause some problems. When many people from the city move to a village, the house prices goes up, and local young people cannot afford to buy a home. Also, the internet in the countryside is sometimes slow, and there are less hospitals and other services.

In conclusion, I believe that people moving from cities to the countryside because of remote work is a positive development. It gives people a better quality of life and brings new life to small towns. However, the government should improve internet and services in rural area.
samples.why: Clear positive position · relevant ideas for individuals and communities with limited development · simple linking · adequate vocabulary · several agreement errors and a quantifier error that do not affect clarity.

samples.text:
The rise of remote working has allowed many employees to leave expensive cities and settle in smaller towns and rural areas. In my view, this movement is a positive development, both for the individuals concerned and for the places they move to.

For the people who relocate, the improvement in quality of life can be considerable. City living often involves high housing costs, long commutes and limited green space. By moving to a smaller community, remote workers can usually afford more spacious homes, spend the time they once lost travelling with their families, and enjoy a calmer environment. Many report that this balance between work and personal life makes them healthier and more productive.

The trend can also help to revive rural areas. For decades, young people have moved away from the countryside in search of employment, leaving behind ageing populations and declining services. New residents who keep their city salaries bring spending power to local businesses, and their children help to keep village schools open. At the same time, a reduction in population pressure can ease congestion and housing shortages in overcrowded cities.

Admittedly, this migration creates some tensions. In popular areas, the arrival of wealthier newcomers has pushed up property prices, making it harder for local people to stay in the communities where they grew up. Rural infrastructure, such as broadband and public transport, may also struggle to cope with a growing population. However, these are problems that careful planning, such as building affordable homes for local residents and investing in digital connections, can address.

In conclusion, although the movement of remote workers to smaller towns needs to be managed carefully, it offers a better quality of life for many people and new energy for struggling rural communities. Overall, I see it as a positive trend.
samples.why: Clear position throughout · benefits for individuals and communities well extended · problems acknowledged and answered · clear central topics and good cohesion · good collocations (spending power, population pressure) · largely error-free.

samples.text:
Freed from the obligation to commute daily to an office, a significant number of professionals have left large cities for market towns, coastal villages and the countryside. Although this migration has created real difficulties in some places, I believe that its overall effect is positive.

The benefits for those who move are the most immediate. Residents of major cities frequently pay a large share of their income for cramped accommodation and spend hours each week travelling to work. Relocating allows them to exchange these costs for more space, cleaner air and closer contact with nature, while continuing to earn a city salary. For families in particular, this can mean more time together and a less pressured daily routine.

More significantly, the trend has the potential to reverse a long-standing imbalance between urban and rural areas. For generations, economic opportunity has been concentrated in a few large cities, drawing young people away from smaller communities and leaving them with shrinking populations and disappearing services. Remote workers bring income that circulates through local shops, cafes and tradespeople, and their presence can justify investment in schools, transport and broadband. Meanwhile, cities themselves may benefit from slightly reduced pressure on housing and transport.

The principal drawback is the effect on housing in desirable rural areas. When buyers with urban salaries compete for a limited supply of homes, prices can rise beyond the reach of local families, and young people may be forced to leave the very places that newcomers are moving into. This is a serious concern, but it reflects a failure of housing policy rather than a flaw in the trend itself, and it can be mitigated by building more homes and prioritising local buyers.

In conclusion, provided that its impact on local housing is managed responsibly, the movement of remote workers away from large cities improves individual wellbeing and helps to rebalance regional economies. I therefore consider it a positive development.
samples.why: Clear, qualified positive judgement · ideas fully extended at individual and national level · drawback weighed persuasively · seamless cohesion · wide, natural vocabulary (rebalance, circulates) · error-free, wide range of structures.
